content.passage: I was enjoying breakfast in the dining room of my brother's house, when his wife Rose came into the room. 'When are you going to do anything useful, Rudolf?' she asked. 'My dear Rose, why should I do anything? I have money and a good family. My brother is Lord Burlesdon and you are his charming wife. It is enough!' 'You are twenty-nine, and all you have done is-' 'Travel? That's true. But our family doesn't need to do things.' Rose looked annoyed. She thought that I was lazy. This was true, but I had traveled and learned a lot. I spoke German perfectly. I was a good swordsman, and I could ride a horse well. Now, Sir Jacob Borrodaile was offering me work as an ambassador in six months' time. I decided to visit Ruritania, where King Rudolf V was soon to be crowned.

content.script: Presenter: Welcome to today's literature overview of 'The Prisoner of Zenda' by Anthony Hope. The novel tells the thrilling adventure of Rudolf Rassendyll, an English gentleman who travels to Ruritania. Upon arrival, he meets the real King, Rudolf V, who looks almost identical to him. When the King is drugged by his half-brother Duke Michael on the eve of the coronation, Rudolf is persuaded by loyal officers Sapt and Fritz to impersonate the King at Strelsau to save the crown.
